title: Nehemiah 1
paragraphs: ¹ These are the words of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was at the citadel of Susa ² when Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some other men from Judah. I asked them about the Jewish remnant that had survived the exile, and about Jerusalem. ³ They told me, "The survivors there in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down and its gates have been burned." ⁴ When I heard this, I sat down and wept. For several days I mourned and fasted and prayed to the God of heaven. ⁵ I said, "LORD, God of heaven, great and awesome God, who keeps his covenant of love with those who love him and obey his commands,

⁶ let your ear be attentive and your eyes open, so that you may hear the prayer I am praying to you day and night for your servants, the people of Israel. I confess the sins we have committed against you — both I and my father's house have sinned. ⁷ We have acted wickedly toward you and have not obeyed the commands, statutes, and decrees you gave your servant Moses. ⁸ Remember what you told Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations, ⁹ but if you return to me and obey my commands, then even if your exiled people are at the farthest horizon, I will gather them from there and bring them to the place I have chosen as a dwelling for my Name.' ¹⁰ These are your servants, your people, whom you redeemed by your great strength and your mighty hand.

¹¹ Lord, let your ear be attentive to the prayer of your servant and to the prayer of your servants who delight in honoring your name. Give your servant success today and grant him mercy in the presence of this man." I was the king's cupbearer.
